explanation: 该论文主要关注非洲城市中基于自然的解决方案，涉及气候行动和城市环境，但未提及大气环境遥感技术、空气质量监测、卫星观测或大气成分分析等关键术语。
authors: Nicola Frances Rule;Cameron T McLean;Andrew Emmanuel Okem;Promise M Nduku;Johannes Bhanye;Collins Matiza;Fred Sato;Chipo Perseverance Mungenge;Onyekachi Esther Ogunniyi;Ignacio Pita-Vaca;Cherié Janine Forbes;Petra Holden;Christopher H Trisos;Debra C Roberts;Nicholas P Simpson
title: A systematic review of nature-based solutions for climate action in African cities
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS), including ecosystem-based adaptation, are increasingly proposed for climate action in African cities, but the evidence base is fragmented and lacks systematic synthesis of what is being implemented, where, and how effectively. We analysed 112 studies retained from a systematic review, covering 134 urban areas across 42 countries and including 45 informal settlements. Five NbS typology classes are inductively derived including: Green spaces; Rivers, catchments and drainage systems; Coastal systems; Green buildings; and Urban agriculture and multi-use gardens. Urban green spaces dominate the evidence (49% of studies) and are the most multi-functional class. Urban agriculture and multi-use gardens are under-recognised in headline framings, named as primary in only 5% of studies but appearing in 34% of the wider intervention mix. Evidence is increasing but concentrates geographically on larger cities. Successful climate change adaptation and mitigation outcomes are reported by 72% and 27% of studies, respectively. Heat mitigation is the most frequently quantified adaptation outcome, with temperature reductions up to 12.2 °C reported in proximity to urban green and blue spaces across the continent. Qualitative evidence links urban NbS to effective coastal protection, flood risk reduction, and increased water security. Multi-stakeholder governance anchored by local actors, and meaningful community participation are consistent enablers of effective implementation. However, insufficient long-term funding and livelihood disruptions and displacement raise concerns about long-term impacts. Priority research gaps include longitudinal effectiveness monitoring, financing mechanisms for informal contexts, systematic assessment of mechanisms behind inequitable outcomes, and evidence from under-represented regions and smaller cities.

explanation: 该论文使用卫星数据（NDVI）分析热干旱对森林恢复力的影响，涉及物种多样性和环境因素，属于大气环境遥感技术（如卫星观测和森林生态系统分析）的范畴。
authors: Zifan Zhang;Pei Wang;Xiuchen Wu;Wen Zhang;Yang Li;Renjie Guo;Xiaona Wang;Zekai Meng
title: Hot drought reshapes the relationship between tree species diversity and forest resilience
abstract: Climate warming is increasing the occurrence of hot droughts, in which water deficits coincide with anomalously high temperatures, posing growing risks to forest ecosystems and carbon sequestration. Yet whether tree species diversity (TSD) affects forest resilience differently under drought-only and hot drought remains unclear. Here, we conducted a global assessment of TSD effects on NDVI-based forest resilience following drought-only and hot drought events. By integrating satellite-based estimates of resilience with global tree species richness data and environmental factors across ten major forest biomes, we found that global forests exhibited reduced post-drought growth under both drought conditions, with more spatially extensive reductions under hot drought. Importantly, the TSD-resilience relationship differed markedly between the two drought types. TSD effects on forest resilience were widely negative under drought-only conditions but were predominantly positive under hot drought. Hot drought also amplified both positive and negative TSD effects relative to drought-only events. Interaction analyses further showed that, under drought-only conditions, TSD effects were broadly modulated by mean annual temperature and vapor pressure deficit, whereas under hot drought, mean annual temperature was the only environmental variable showing widespread modulation of TSD effects. In addition, resilience was more sensitive to the number of tree species under hot drought and in species-poor forests. Our findings highlight that anomalously high temperature accompanying drought reshapes both the direction and magnitude of TSD effects on forest resilience and identify low-richness regions as strategic targets where management interventions may deliver greater ecological benefits.

explanation: 该论文研究了2025年欧洲极端热浪的成因，重点关注大气环流和人为强迫对高温条件的影响。虽然未直接提及遥感技术，但其涉及大气成分分析（温度异常）、气候变化归因等与遥感技术密切相关的研究内容，因此判定为强相关。
authors: Yan Chen;Wen Chen;Shangfeng Chen;Juan Feng;Tianjiao Ma
title: Role of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the extreme 2025 European summer heatwave
abstract: In summer 2025, an extreme heatwave propagated northeastward across Europe, sequentially affecting Southwestern (SWEU) and Northern (NEU) Europe with record-breaking durations in the 1979–2025 record. However, the roles of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the 2025 European high-temperature conditions remain unclear. Here we show that atmospheric circulation explains 82.5% (95% uncertainty interval: 65.0%–99.0%) and 51.9% (37.0%–65.2%) of the regional mean maximum temperature (Tmax) anomalies averaged over the respective heatwave periods in SWEU and NEU, respectively, based on the flow analogue method. Extreme anticyclonic circulation is associated with extreme Arctic Oscillation and British–Baikal Corridor (BBC) patterns in SWEU, and BBC and Atlantic–Eurasia patterns in NEU. Detection and attribution using Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 simulations show that anthropogenic forcing increases the probability of exceeding the European mean June-July Tmax level observed in 2025 by a factor of 194.0 (95% confidence interval: 128.3–298.6). Greenhouse gas forcing increases the likelihood of exceeding this threshold, whereas anthropogenic aerosol forcing reduces it. These results provide insights into the roles of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in European high-temperature conditions.

explanation: 该论文使用多时相和多传感器的遥感技术来制作咖啡分布图，并评估其对欧盟防森林砍伐法规的影响。这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，特别是卫星观测和土地利用变化分析。
authors: Tin W Satriawan;Xiangzhong Luo;Shafira Nur Ramdhania;Agustín Escobar-López;Anggun Tridawati
title: Nearly ninety percent of Indonesian coffee area is classified as deforestation-free under the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)
abstract: Indonesia is the third-largest coffee producer globally and exports a substantial share of its production to European Union (EU) countries. Recent implementation of the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which requires deforestation-free supply chains, highlights the need for spatially-explicit coffee mapping to support the assessment of coffee-associated deforestation. In this study, we utilized multitemporal and multi-sensor remote sensing to produce annual maps of coffee distribution from 2016 to 2024. We analyzed the spatial patterns of annual coffee distribution during this period, and evaluated the potential implications of EUDR for coffee production in Indonesia. Our maps of coffee agroecosystems demonstrate an overall classification accuracy exceeding 80%, and are broadly consistent with independent coffee datasets (i.e. national statistics and coffee probability maps from the Forest Data Partnership). We detected a net increase of ∼16% in coffee area over the eight-year period, although the patterns of change vary across provinces. Based on these findings, we estimate that 87.9% of the mapped coffee area in 2024 meets the EUDR deforestation-free criterion, and only a relatively small proportion of agroecosystems are classified as non-deforestation-free. These findings highlight opportunities for spatially targeted EUDR implementation, where deforestation-free coffee agroecosystems can be supported towards meeting broader EUDR requirements, while areas associated with forest conversion can be supported towards other pathways, such as sustainable agricultural practices, restoration, and forest conservation.

explanation: 该论文研究了亚马逊雨林夜间边界层（NBL）的观测复杂动力学和CO2传输，使用了CloudRoots-Amazon22观测数据，并与理想化模型进行了对比。这涉及到大气环境遥感和空气成分分析，因此与题目要求的相关性较高。
authors: Anna C. Huitema;Vincent S. de Feiter;Raquel González-Armas;Oscar K. Hartogensis;Hella van Asperen;Cleo Q. Dias-Júnior;Jordi Vilà-Guerau de Arellano
title: From prototypical regimes to observed complex dynamics and CO2 transport in the Amazonian nocturnal boundary layer
abstract:
We studied how well idealised models of the nighttime boundary layer capture observed variability above the Amazon rainforest, using observations from the CloudRoots-Amazon22 campaign. The observations indicate large nocturnal variability, caused by non-stationary processes and interactions between the within- and above-canopy atmosphere. Common weather and climate models often miss this variability, highlighting the need to represent the complex forest-atmosphere interactions better. 
 We investigated the characteristics of the nocturnal boundary layer (NBL) above and within the Amazon rainforest canopy during the 2022 dry season. We analysed observed NBL dynamics and CO2 transport from the perspective of the prototypical NBL represented in weather and climate models. To this end, using the CloudRoots-Amazon22 dataset, we characterised the main NBL features and governing processes. We identified NBL height using five methods based on thermal stratification, wind, and turbulent criteria, finding a distinct stable layer above the canopy with an average height between 142–164 m. To examine the drivers of the dynamic NBL evolution, we classified the data into weakly and strongly stable regimes, determined by the interplay between stabilising longwave radiative cooling and destabilising mechanical wind shear. Budget equations for turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), heat, and CO2 allowed us to quantify the relative contributions of these drivers to transport across the canopy-atmosphere interface. In the weakly stable regime, increased TKE at the canopy top promoted mixing between the within- and above-canopy layers. Conversely, TKE was nearly absent in the strongly stable regime, decoupling the two layers. This decoupling favoured strong thermal stratification above the canopy and well-mixed conditions within the canopy. Our results show that only about 6 % of observed profiles conform to prototypical NBL regimes, emphasising the need to revisit parameterisations to explicitly account for canopy-induced effects and intermittent turbulence. Our observational analysis provides a critical benchmark for improving the representation of NBL dynamics and CO2 transport in models.

explanation: 该论文研究了利用氡（radon）来改进甲烷（methane）排放估计的方法，通过双重示踪剂反演（dual-tracer inversion）技术，旨在提高甲烷通量估计的可靠性。这涉及到大气传输模型和温室气体排放估计，与大气环境遥感技术（如大气成分分析、排放监测）密切相关，因此该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Fabian Maier;Christian Rödenbeck;Ute Karstens;Frank-Thomas Koch;Maksym Gachkivskyi;Andrew Smerald;Christoph Gerbig
title: Can radon help to improve methane emission estimates? Results from a dual-tracer inversion
abstract:
Transport model errors represent a major source of uncertainty in greenhouse gas flux estimates derived from inverse modelling, yet they remain challenging to quantify. In our study, we leverage the similarities in the atmospheric transport of methane (CH4) and radon (222Rn) by performing a dual-tracer CH4-222Rn inversion over Europe, with the goal of enhancing the reliability of CH4 flux estimates. We discuss the benefits and limitations of this dual-tracer approach. 
 A major source of uncertainty in inverse modelling of greenhouse gas emissions are deficits in atmospheric transport models, in particular in the description of vertical mixing within the planetary boundary layer (PBL). The properties of radon-222 (Rn) makes it a suitable natural tracer for vertical mixing in the PBL. When comparing the CH4 model-data mismatch (MDM), i.e. the differences between the observed and modelled CH4 concentrations, with the MDM of Rn, we found substantial correlations for several observation sites in central Europe in 2021 (the median CH4-Rn MDM correlation coefficient is 0.6), indicating that a large part of the CH4 and Rn MDM variability can be explained by common errors in the simulated (vertical) transport. We aim to exploit this information in a joint inversion for CH4 and Rn by taking into account prior uncertainties and making use of the fact that the transport model error is correlated between the two gases. We use simultaneous CH4 and Rn observations from 17 sites across central Europe in 2021. The dual-tracer CH4-Rn inversion yields lower CH4 fluxes in several countries covered by the observation sites compared to a single-tracer CH4-only inversion without Rn information. The differences in country-total CH4 fluxes between the dual-tracer and single-tracer inversions are on the order of a few percent and depend on the assumed uncertainty for the Rn prior fluxes. These findings underscore the importance of accurate Rn flux maps for fully leveraging the dual-tracer approach and enhancing the reliability of CH4 flux estimates.

explanation: 该论文研究从实测数据中推导积云云底的饱和水汽过饱和度，属于大气环境遥感技术中的大气成分分析范畴，涉及云物理和热力学过程，与空气质量监测和卫星观测相关。
topic_words: ['water vapor supersaturation', 'cumulus cloud base', 'in situ measurements', 'atmospheric thermodynamics']
authors: Ramon C. Braga;Manfred Wendisch;Rachel Albrecht;Daniel Harrison
title: A new method to derive water vapor supersaturation at cumulus cloud base from in situ measurements
abstract:
We introduce a new thermodynamic framework to derive water vapor supersaturation at warm cumulus cloud base from in situ measurements. The framework describes the local transition between saturated thermodynamic states as an adiabatic and reversible process under quasi-isobaric conditions, in which the latent energy released during condensation is partitioned between changes in internal energy and water-vapor expansion work. 
 Current in situ measurements of water vapor supersaturation (Sv) with respect to liquid water at cloud base are highly uncertain due to instrumental limitations. Consequently, Sv is commonly estimated using cloud microphysical models and parameterizations. Here, we derive Sv at warm cumulus cloud base from in situ measurements through calculations of the energy and water vapor budgets associated with cloud formation. The derived Sv provides a thermodynamic analogue to the supersaturation established in a cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) chamber, enabling direct comparison with independently measured CCN activation spectra below cloud base. To this end, we formulate the energy budget of a saturated rising air parcel at cloud base and treat the transition between saturated thermodynamic states locally as quasi-isobaric. Under these conditions, the latent heat (Q) released during condensational droplet growth is determined by the corresponding sensible enthalpy difference between the saturated-vapor and water vapor–liquid states. According to the first law of thermodynamics, Q is partitioned between the change in internal energy (ΔU) and water vapor expansion work (Ws). Within this diagnostic framework, part of the condensational energy is, therefore, spent on Ws, reducing the amount of liquid water formed relative to the limiting case in which the entire condensational energy contributes to droplet growth. Accordingly, the cloud supersaturation (Sc) is diagnostically partitioned into liquid-phase (Sl) and vapor-phase (Sv) components based on the fractions of Q associated with ΔU and Ws, respectively. This framework enables the derivation of Sv from airborne cloud-base measurements through thermodynamic constraints on condensational energy partitioning. Here we use airborne measurements collected in growing convective cumuli over the Amazon Basin during the ACRIDICON-CHUVA campaign. Our results demonstrate that the derived cloud droplet number concentration as a function of Sv agrees, within measurement uncertainties, with Sv activation spectra of CCN measured below cloud base.

explanation: 该研究关注苯和苯酚等芳香族化合物在大气中的二次有机气溶胶形成机制，涉及大气化学动力学、空气质量模型和气溶胶演化等关键内容，与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测和气溶胶分析密切相关。
authors: Aurélien Le Bayon;Aliisa Ojala;Siddharth Iyer;Zhizhao Wang;Victor Lannuque;Florian Couvidat;Raluca Ciuraru;Karine Sartelet
title: Molecular representation of benzene and phenol secondary organic aerosols
abstract:
Aromatics compounds emitted in the atmosphere, such as benzene and phenol, contribute to the formation of organic aerosols. This study presents and evaluates an updated description of benzene chemistry, in which the most influential pathways are identified, including one developed in this work. The resulting mechanism reproduces laboratory observation with great accuracy and is reduced for use in large-scale air quality models. 
 Recent experimental and theoretical work has highlighted missing pathways in the oxidation of aromatic compounds, with consequences for the formation of highly oxygenated products relevant to secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation. In this study we develop an updated, quasi-explicit oxidation mechanism for benzene based on Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM) v3.3.1, extended to represent key multi-generation chemistry. Quantum chemical calculations are used to derive the formation and evolution of geminal-diol bicyclic peroxy radicals and to parameterize the subsequent molecular rearrangements. The mechanism further incorporates autoxidation sequences previously developed for peroxy and alkoxy radicals, successive OH additions and cyclic epoxides formation. This approach enables a more mechanistic description of aromatic oxidation leading to highly oxygenated, low-volatility products. The mechanism is evaluated using box-model simulations against a set of chamber experiments conducted under various conditions. Simulated aerosol concentrations agree well with observations and emphasize the dominant contribution of the newly implemented pathways. The quasi-explicit mechanism is subsequently reduced using the GENerator of reduced Organic Aerosol mechanisms (GENOA), resulting in a semi-explicit mechanism reduced to 1 % of its original number of species while reproducing SOA mass with a mean error of 3.9 % relative to the quasi-explicit scheme. Using the validated reduced mechanism, zero-dimensional simulations under contrasted atmospheric conditions are conducted to estimate the SOA compounds that are formed in the early stages of oxidation and those that dominate the system at later stages.

explanation: 该论文研究的是利用毫米波云雷达观测雾的能见度，涉及大气成分分析和遥感技术，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Xiaojie Li;Jinming Ge;Yucheng Qiu;Qiaoyi Lv;Wei Song;Jie Zhang;Chi Zhang;Bochun Liu;Jiapeng Wang;Hongwei Xia;Yuhang Zhu
title: Physically constrained retrieval of fog visibility from millimeter-wavelength cloud radar observations
abstract:
Fog threatens transportation but is hard to monitor. Ground sensors see only single points and satellites miss vertical detail. We developed a radar-based method to estimate visibility inside fog based on how fog droplets block light. The method finds water content and droplet sizes from radar signals, then calculates how far one can see. It provides three-dimensional fog monitoring without extra instruments. 
 Fog severely degrades visibility (Vis) and poses substantial risks to transportation and aviation, yet quantitative monitoring remains challenging because conventional ground-based instruments provide spatially limited point observations and cannot resolve three-dimensional fog structure, while passive satellite retrievals have insufficient vertical resolution and difficulty separating fog from low cloud. Millimeter-wavelength cloud radar (MMCR) can penetrate fog and provide fine spatiotemporal resolution, but many radar Vis retrievals rely on empirical reflectivity–visibility relations. This study develops a physically constrained, observation-calibrated single-wavelength Ka-band MMCR retrieval that links reflectivity, liquid water content (LWC), geometric median radius, extinction, and Vis through lognormal droplet-size-distribution moments. A segment-wise mass-absorption LWC power law and an extinction-oriented radius power law are fitted to same-source FM-120 extinction-matching pseudo-targets, achieving a mean absolute fractional extinction error of 9.37 % on the development dataset. In ten spring-2025 DNQ3-conditioned cases, the present retrieval attains a mean absolute error of 0.092 km, while the local FM-120 and Liu et al. (2019) relations yield broadly comparable ranges and the Gultepe et al. (2009) relation departs more strongly. This method improves the physical self-consistency of single-band MMCR fog Vis retrieval without requiring auxiliary in-situ observations and provides technical support for three-dimensional coastal fog monitoring and traffic meteorological early warning.

explanation: 该论文研究了EUMETSAT的Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager（MTG-LI）的性能，这是一个用于监测闪电活动的地球静止轨道光学位移系统。闪电是大气化学和气象学的重要指标，因此该研究直接与大气环境遥感技术相关，特别是与闪电监测和大气成分分析相关。
topic_words: ['Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager', 'lightning detection', 'geostationary lightning location system', 'atmospheric chemistry']
authors: Bartolomeo Viticchié;Sven-Erik Enno;David Navia;Janja Avbelj;Jochen Grandell
title: Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager detection performances
abstract:
Lightning is a vital meteorological indicator, an Essential Climate Variable, and a key factor in atmospheric chemistry. EUMETSAT’s Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager (MTG-LI), operational since July 2024, is Europe’s first space-based geostationary lightning location system devoted to lightning diagnosis and characterization. This manuscript assesses its performance over 18 months, serving as a foundational reference for users. 
 The EUMETSAT Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager (MTG-LI) is the European space-based geostationary lightning location system devoted to the diagnosis and characterization of lightning activity over hemispheric scale. In this publication, we present the assessment of MTG-LI detection performances against four different reference systems: the Vaisala Global Lightning Detection Network (GLD360), the European Cooperation for Lightning Detection (EUCLID), and Geostationary Lightning Mappers (GLMs) −16 and −19 aboard NOAA GOES satellites. The analysis period is eighteen months: from July 2024 to December 2025. MTG-LI absolute flash detection efficiency varies between 70 % (day) and 95 % (night), with an average value of 87.4 %. Its average flash  false  alarm  rate  is  generally below 0.5 flash s−1, while the average fraction of false flashes is 0.16 % of the total flashes. Finally, both average timing and location accuracy are presented and discussed.

explanation: 该论文主要关注古海平面指标和南亚及印度洋地区的海岸线变化，涉及地质年代、沉积环境和大地构造，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）的关联性较弱。
authors: Mubashir Ali;Ciro Cerrone;Alessio Rovere
title: A review of Last Interglacial sea-level proxies  in South Asia and the Indian Ocean
abstract:
We compiled a database of 54 ancient shoreline markers from Iran, Oman, India, the Maldives and the Cocos Islands, dating to Marine Isotopic Stage 5. The records show that the same past ocean level can appear far above today's sea on rising coasts, near today's level on stable coasts, and many meters underwater where land is sinking. This helps separate true ocean change from land motion and improves future sea-level planning. 
 In this work, we present a standardized database of Last Interglacial (LIG, ∼132–80 ka) sea-level proxies across the South Asian and Indian Ocean region, including the coasts of Iran, Oman, India, the Maldives, and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands. The database stems from a systematic review of the data included in 17 peer-reviewed studies, structured according to the World Atlas of Last Interglacial Shorelines (WALIS), and is available as Ali et al. (2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18512769). Within this framework, a total of 54 sea-level index points were re-evaluated to recalculate paleo-RSL elevation and associated uncertainties. This was achieved through updated determinations of their indicative meaning (i.e., reference water level and indicative range), considering the original stratigraphic context, elevation measurement techniques, depositional environments, and chronological constraints. The chronological framework relies on U-Th, luminescence, electron spin resonance, and cosmogenic nuclide dating. These data are characterized by regional differences in the elevation of past relative sea-level proxies that are driven primarily by tectonics, dynamic topography, and glacio-hydro-isostatic forcings. On the active margins of southern Iran and northern Oman, marine terraces dated to Marine Isotope Stage (MIS) 5e (∼125 ka), 5c (∼100 ka), and 5a (∼80 ka) are preserved at 20–60 m a.s.l., reflecting uplift linked to the Zagros foreland and Makran subduction system at least since the Last Interglacial. On the coasts of western and southern India, MIS 5e relative sea-level proxies are found at 1–4 m a.s.l., more in line with near-zero vertical land motion. On Indian Ocean islands, such as the Maldives and Cocos (Keeling) Islands, MIS 5e reefs are now submerged at depths of 10–17 m b.s.l., indicating subsidence since the LIG.

explanation: 该论文主要研究古代人类和动物的稳定同位素分析，以揭示其饮食、居住地和迁徙距离，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关联。
authors: Anna Hagarová;Margarita Gorbulina;Kévin Salesse
title: Stable isotope bioarchaeological atlas from the post-Soviet space
abstract:
Chemical traces in ancient bones and teeth reveal what people ate, where they lived, and how far they travelled. We compiled results from over a hundred studies, spanning more than one hundred thousand years across the former Soviet space, much published only in Russian and largely absent from international literature. The result is a large, open collection of ancient human and animal remains from Asia and the Caucasus, now freely accessible to researchers worldwide. 
 Results of stable isotope analyses from 435 locations in the countries of the former USSR were collected from 114 papers presenting the results of their research and compiled in two datasets stored in the IsoArcH database. The literature research was conducted using Google Scholar, Web of Science and Science Direct using keywords both in English and in other relevant languages, such as Russian, Ukrainian, Azerbaijani, Georgian or Kazakh. The datasets contain information on the originating site, including GPS coordinates, information on the samples (as available) such as source of origin, dating and details of deposition, and results of stable isotope analysis, namely the measurements of carbon (δ13C), nitrogen (δ15N), oxygen (δ18O), sulphur (δ34S) strontium (87Sr//86Sr) and lead (206Pb/204Pb). All source articles are connected to relevant data within the datasets. This compilation can serve as a comprehensive source for further research as well as a reference set for the geographical and temporal area.

explanation: 该论文研究的是一种拉格朗日粒子追踪框架，用于模拟云中粒子的生长和合并，涉及大气微物理过程，这是大气环境遥感技术中的一个重要研究方向。虽然论文没有直接提到空气质量监测或卫星观测，但其对粒子追踪和模拟的研究与大气成分分析、气溶胶检索等领域密切相关。
topic_words: ['Lagrangian particle tracking', 'cloud particles', 'super-droplet simulations', 'atmospheric microphysics', 'particle-based models']
authors: Chongzhi Yin;Shin-Ichiro Shima;Chunsong Lu
title: A Lagrangian particle tracking framework for the  super-droplet method in SCALE-SDM 5.2.6-2.3.1:  implementation and computational evaluation
abstract:
We developed and tested a way to trace selected cloud particles in a simulation, including how they grow and merge. One run identifies particles that meet chosen conditions, and a second reconstructs only their saved histories. In a three-dimensional test, the saved data were estimated to be one-fifth of what would be needed to keep all particle histories. Larger reductions are possible when fewer particles are selected, making such studies more practical in large simulations. 
 Lagrangian particle histories provide a useful way to diagnose cloud-microphysical pathways in particle-based models, but their practical use in massively parallel super-droplet simulations depends on how particle identifiers, event records, output files, and post-processing workflows are implemented. This paper documents and evaluates a Lagrangian particle-tracking framework in SCALE-SDM 5.2.6-2.3.1. The framework includes forward tracking, backward tracking, and Two-Pass Hybrid Tracking (TPHT). Forward tracking saves the later states of super-droplets selected before or during a simulation. Backward tracking saves the rank and record location of each selected super-droplet's predecessor at the previous output time, so that post-processing can retrieve that record with an 𝒪(1) lookup instead of searching all super-droplets. Both methods use a common procedure to select all valid super-droplets, a random or height–radius-stratified sample, or an externally supplied target list. TPHT uses two integrations over the same physical time interval. The first records super-droplet identifiers when a chosen radius or coalescence condition is met. After duplicate identifiers are removed, the second starts from the same physical and random-number state and writes backward links only for this reduced set. Controlled computational tests are used to characterise runtime, peak random-access memory (RAM), storage (disk-output volume), the effect of output interval on file volume and mean write time, and sampling error and seed-to-seed variability. A three-dimensional DYCOMS-II RF02 stratocumulus case demonstrates TPHT. In this demonstration, the target criteria selected 19.3 % of the estimated valid super-droplet identities, corresponding to an estimated 5.2-fold reduction in retained backward output after temporary identifier files were removed. This factor is specific to the broad criteria used in this test; much larger reductions are possible for problems with sparser target populations. Agreement of the recorded coalescence events between the two integrations provided evidence of reproducibility under the tested configuration. The case study shows that TPHT can identify particles of interest and reconstruct their saved histories while reducing retained output. In future, the same approach could be applied to other history- or event-based questions, including entrainment and mixing, sedimentation, and ice-particle growth.

title: Degradation Rate and Lifetime of Small Impact Craters on the Moon
abstract: Knowledge of crater degradation rates on the Moon is fundamental for dating individual craters, understanding material transport, and investigating crater equilibrium, with broader implications for water ice exploration, regolith evolution, and impact flux reconstruction. However, direct observational constraints on the degradation rates of hundred‐meter‐scale lunar craters remain scarce, and regional variations between mare and highland terrains are poorly quantified. Here, we measure the diameters and depths of 56,229 small impact craters across the Apollo, Luna, and Chang’E landing regions using high‐resolution optical and topographic data. We then systematically simulate the production and evolution of crater populations from geological unit emplacement to the present, accounting for both diffusive degradation and catastrophic obliteration. By comparing observations with forward simulations, we provide the most extensive observational constraints to date on the degradation rates and lifetimes of small craters with diameters of 50–500 m. At these scales, the estimated topographic diffusivities increase from 0.62 to 2.33 m2 ${\mathrm{m}}^{2}$/Myr in the maria and from 2.27 to 4.54 m2 ${\mathrm{m}}^{2}$/Myr in the highlands. Regional variations in degradation rates are most strongly associated with meter‐scale slope rather than adopted proxies for target properties. The inferred lifetimes imply that subhectometer micro cold traps are short‐lived (<100 Myr) and thus host only recently delivered water ice, whereas larger cold traps of several hundred meters can persist over geological timescales and are favorable for water ice accumulation. Our results further indicate that crater equilibrium at small diameters is achieved mainly through diffusive degradation rather than superposition, and that equilibrium crater abundance is expected to vary across the Moon.

authors: Sandro W. Lubis;L. Ruby Leung;J. Michael Battalio
title: More Frequent Atmospheric Rivers and Associated Precipitation Extremes Induced by the Baroclinic Annular Mode
abstract: Atmospheric rivers (ARs) play a crucial role in the global hydrological cycle, yet how the intrinsic midlatitude atmospheric variability modulates their activity on subseasonal timescales remains poorly understood. Here, we show that AR frequency and landfall in both hemispheres vary strongly with the strength and phase of the Baroclinic Annular Mode (BAM). During its positive phase, BAM increases AR occurrence by up to ∼50% and AR‐driven precipitation extremes by up to ∼40% relative to climatology. Stronger and more frequent ARs during the positive phase of the BAM are primarily driven by enhanced potential‐to‐kinetic energy conversion, which favors AR growth and intensification, particularly in the storm‐track regions. This response is consistent with dynamically enhanced poleward moisture transport due to a more baroclinically unstable and stormier environment. The results underscore the importance of BAM‐related intrinsic midlatitude storm‐track variability in modulating global AR activity and its potential to improve extended‐range AR prediction on subseasonal timescales.

title: How Microporosity Shapes Carbonate Hydraulic Behavior: A Digital Rock Physics Perspective
abstract: Carbonate hydraulic behavior emerges from flow through pore structures spanning resolvable macropores and sub‐resolution microporous regions, yet the effects of microporosity level and heterogeneity remain poorly understood. We develop and validate a CUDA‐accelerated lattice Boltzmann model that unifies pore‐resolved and continuum flow. Simulations show that low‐velocity microporous regions substantially contribute to bulk flow by activating connections between macropores. Across three carbonate samples, permeability increases nonlinearly with microporosity, with reference permeabilities spanning over two orders of magnitude. Moreover, at fixed bulk porosity, amplifying the observed phase‐wise contrast increases permeability, while spatial permutation controls reveal a dominant contribution from the original spatial organization. Three‐dimensional spatial and pressure‐gradient analyses further indicate that high‐microporosity phases preferentially adjacent to macropores become increasingly conductive as heterogeneity increases, reducing local flow resistance. These results show how naturally organized microporosity controls hydraulic behavior and bulk permeability in multiscale geological porous media.

title: Decadal Creep Acceleration on the Northern Japan Trench Driven by Erosion of Heterogeneously Locked Asperities
abstract: Geodetic and seismic observations before the 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku‐oki earthquake indicate decadal‐scale acceleration of aseismic slip along the northern Japan Trench, but the mechanism remains debated. We show that this transient can be explained by creep‐front propagation that progressively erodes heterogeneously locked asperities. We invert GNSS velocity fields from 1998 to 2009 using a mechanically motivated model in which locked regions are confined to historical rupture areas while their effective sizes and process‐zone stressing rates evolve. The models fit both velocity fields and predict slip accelerations consistent with repeating‐earthquake estimates. Inferred asperities occupied about 66% of their corresponding rupture areas in 1998 and about 37% in 2009, indicating substantial expansion of aseismic creep over the decade before rupture. The inferred shrinkage rates are consistent with fracture‐mechanics predictions for plausible coseismic stress drops. These results suggest that megathrust locking can evolve substantially over decadal timescales.

authors: Zhenwei Liu;Chuan Huang;Jinru Cheng;Tangsheng Cheng;Hang Zhou;Chaomei Wu;Chen Liang;Tingdi Chen;Weilong Luo;Chong Wang;Zhaofeng Wang;Ruocan Zhao;Xianghui Xue
title: Seasonal and Diurnal Variability of Thermospheric Metastable Helium Observed by Multi‐Platform Observations and Numerical Modeling
abstract: Metastable helium (He∗ ${\text{He}}^{\ast }$) in the thermosphere emits at 1,083 nm and provides a powerful diagnostic of thermospheric composition, solar radiation, and transport. Its detection remains challenging because of its extremely low density and high‐altitude. Here, we present the first multi‐platform study of thermospheric He∗ ${\text{He}}^{\ast }$ variability using a He∗ ${\text{He}}^{\ast }$ density model, ground‐based LiDAR observations over Danzhou, China, and SPHEREx 1,083 nm measurements from May 2025 to April 2026. The three data sets show consistent seasonal variability, with reduced He∗ ${\text{He}}^{\ast }$‐related signals from late spring to midsummer and enhanced values in autumn and winter. Model results associate this pattern with changes in background ground‐state helium reservoir. A representative diurnal case shows the strongest response at 500–700 km, with enhanced values after 04:50 local time. An additional LiDAR‐observed layer above approximately 950 km is not fully captured by the model, highlighting the need for further He∗ ${\text{He}}^{\ast }$ model development. These results provide observational guidance for helium models.

authors: Haozhe He;Brian J. Soden;Ryan J. Kramer
title: Improved Estimates of Equilibrium Climate Sensitivity From Non‐Equilibrated Climate Simulations
abstract: Calculating equilibrium climate sensitivity (ECS) requires simulations of a thousand years or more for the climate to re‐establish equilibrium, but most ECS estimates are derived from shorter model integrations. The widely used “Gregory method” for such estimates systematically underestimates ECS, a bias previously attributed to the time‐dependence of climate feedbacks. Here we demonstrate this underestimate instead arises primarily from an underestimate of radiative forcing. We present a modified method that corrects for the underestimate in forcing, producing ECS estimates that closely align with results from “long‐run” millennium‐scale simulations. This method is robust across models and offers an easily obtainable estimate of ECS with significantly higher accuracy. It enables reliable ECS estimates for full CMIP model ensembles, including models without millennium‐scale simulations. Using this method, we show one of every three CMIP6 climate models has an ECS greater than 5K—the upper bound of the “very likely” range in prior assessments. To further verify this method, we introduce an “integrated feedback parameter” which provides a more physically‐meaningful way to average a time‐evolving climate sensitivity by weighting the differential feedback in consecutive, non‐overlapping time segments by the fraction of energy imbalance that each segment restores. This parameter agrees well with that derived from our modified method, lending further credibility to this simplified approach.

authors: Thomas Oberleitner;Artem Baklanov;Thiago Berton Ferreira;Gerrit Hoogenboom;Jonas Jägermeyr;Atul K. Jain;Tzu‐Shun Lin;Oleksandr Mialyk;Christoph Müller;Alex C. title: Explaining Climatic Drivers of Yield Anomalies in Global Crop Models Through Metamodel‐Based Attribution
abstract: Global gridded crop models (GGCMs) are important tools for assessing climate impacts on agriculture, yet significant divergence in their projections limits interpretability, and impact studies often treat GGCMs as black boxes. Targeted ensemble sensitivity analyses are demanding and not transferable to different ensembles. Here, we comprehensively evaluate climatic and soil drivers of crop yield anomalies in a state‐of‐the‐art GGCM ensemble, using maize as a representative crop. Gradient boosting classifiers detect anomalies, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values quantify feature importance, and methods are applied to a recent GGCM experiment driven by reanalysis climate data. We find broadly similar climatic drivers across the ensemble, though feature importance distributions differ. Low precipitation dominates under rainfed conditions, while solar radiation typically ranks second, highlighting that drought impacts depend on atmospheric water demand often omitted from sensitivity analyses. In some GGCMs, excess rather than insufficient water drives anomalies. The comparison with climate sensitivities derived from a global yield reference data set indicates that no single GGCM performs best across all climate regions. Individual GGCMs may respond well to one climatic stressor but not others, underscoring that bulk benchmarking of GGCMs against observations can obfuscate processes requiring targeted improvement. Our findings demonstrate that evaluating opportunistic data, that is, experiments produced for other purposes, yields vital insights into GGCM divergence in impact studies. Code is publicly available on GitHub to support future attribution analyses and inform broad audiences about drivers of observed results.

authors: Anle Yang;Xiaohui Jiang;Yuxin Lei;Tong Nie;Xujing Li;Shengdong Yang;Fusen Nan;Liangbin Lan
title: Policy‐Driven Evolution of Sediment in the Yellow River Basin over the Past 2000 Years
abstract: River sediment load serves as a typical indicator of the interaction between human activities and the natural environment, and historical policies have profoundly altered basin sediment transport processes. In this study, we constructed a quantitative analytical framework based on the policy index to systematically trace the evolutionary trajectories of ecological conservation, land use, and taxation policies in the Yellow River Basin over the past two millennia. We reveal how policy‐driven human activities have reshaped land use patterns, and how these changes are linked to the long‐term response mechanism of sediment load from the Yellow River. We find that prior to the 1970s, development‐oriented policies promoted cropland expansion via tax incentives and land allocation, leading to vegetation destruction and intensified soil erosion, and sediment load fluctuated and rose to exceed 1.3 Gt/yr. After the 1970s, conservation‐oriented policies restricted development and implemented systematic restoration, causing sediment load to decline to 0.24 Gt/yr in 2020. Human activities contributed 70.56% and 75% of sediment load variation in these two stages, respectively, playing a dominant role, while climate change accounted for less than 30% of the variation in both periods, acting as a periodic regulatory factor. These mechanisms ultimately form the cascading effect of “policies → human activities → land use → sediment load.” The “policy‐response” linkage established in this study provides a quantitative paradigm for understanding millennial‐scale human‐water relationships, and demonstrates the decisive role of policies in river basin governance.

authors: Anyifang Zhang;Ziheng Zhu;Qin Jiang;Quan Yuan;Kaiyue Shan
title: Intensifying Tropical Cyclones and Expanding Renewable Energy Call for Climate‐Resilient Planning in China
abstract: Variable renewable energy (VRE) is central to power system decarbonization for climate mitigation, yet its rapid expansion places growing VRE infrastructure at risk from tropical cyclones (TCs). With TCs projected to intensify, such risks remain poorly quantified at policy‐relevant scales, potentially exposing power systems to unforeseen disruption and damage. Here, we develop a spatially resolved risk projection model by coupling a physics‐based TC hazard module with a power system optimization module to assess the impact of TC climatology change on VRE expansion in China. We find that the TC‐induced economic losses to VRE are projected to increase 10‐ to 20‐fold relative to a historical baseline (1975–2014) of 0.37 billion USD yr−1 by the late 21st century (2061–2100), with wind power accounting for 87%–91% of this increase. The decomposition analysis shows that exposure dominates (contributing 44%–49%) the increase in economic loss growth over 2021–2060, whereas hazard‐exposure interaction dominates (contributing 49%–67%) over 2061–2100. We further identify the optimal strengthening metric, which can offset 54%–67% of the projected economic losses. This framework shifts disaster‐risk assessment from reactive recovery to proactive infrastructure resilience planning, providing a scalable template for climate‐resilient coastal energy transitions worldwide.

authors: O. Tomin;T. Porokhivnyk;A. Juvakoski;O. Varis
title: The Alarming Trend of Water Weaponization During the Russian War in Ukraine
abstract: Water plays a critical role in sustaining civilian populations during armed conflict, yet its deliberate disruption is increasingly reported in contemporary warfare. Despite growing attention to the topic of water weaponization, the concept remains inconsistently defined throughout humanitarian, environmental, and legal literature. This study examines existing conceptualizations of water weaponization and combines them into a broader analytical framework that considers any actions that impair the availability, quality, or accessibility of water for civilian populations as weaponization of water. Using this framework, the study analyzes documented cases from the Russian war in Ukraine and evaluates the limitations of existing international legal mechanisms intended to protect water during armed conflict. The discussion is built on a combination of a scoping literature review and semi‐structured expert interviews. The findings demonstrate that water weaponization extends beyond direct attacks on hydraulic infrastructure and water supply systems, or conflict‐related water pollution. Instead, many consequences arise through indirect impacts and interconnected infrastructure systems. Disruptions to energy, industrial, and water sectors amplify humanitarian and environmental risks that exceed their immediate military significance. The study also reveals persistent challenges in evidence collection, attribution of responsibility, environmental monitoring, and enforcement of existing international legal protections in active conflict settings. By linking empirical evidence from Ukraine with broader debates on water security and conflict, the study contributes to ongoing efforts to clarify the scope of water weaponization and calls for the need to strengthen approaches for assessing water‐related harms during warfare.

title: Cortex-wide imaging in naturally behaving mice with 1-gram wireless mesoscopes
abstract:
Cortex-wide imaging in naturally behaving mice with 1-gram wireless mesoscopes 
 Revealing how distributed cortical circuits coordinate behavior in freely moving animals remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience, constrained by limited fields of view, low throughput, and the tethering required by current miniaturized microscopes1-4. Here, we present Airscope, a wireless mesoscope delivering 4 μm lateral resolution across a 6 mm field of view at 12.5 Hz, weighing 1.0 gram. An aspheric-lens design achieves a 2.84× shorter total track length than previous miniaturized microscopes1,2,5,6 while matching the neuron yield of benchtop one-photon mesoscopes; a tailored wireless link supports cable-free calcium imaging from >8,500 neurons per animal (25‑fold increase). Paired with a zero-shot behavior analyzer, Airscope enables cortical imaging across rich behavioral conditions, including room-scale enriched arenas, swimming assays, and multi-organ implantation, with concurrent recording from multiple animals. Using Airscope, we demonstrate versatile applications of untethered cortical imaging across diverse behavioral paradigms. We identify cortical activity patterns across multiple dorsal regions that correlate with behavioral signatures of social dominance, and show dorsal-cortical population activity prospectively decodes competition outcomes across paired animals. We observe reward-location-associated cortical activity patterns during maze exploration, and characterize Granger-causal influence from spinal cord to cortex during fear conditioning, enabled by simultaneous brain-spinal recordings. By uniting large-scale, cellular-resolution recording with unconstrained behavior, Airscope makes naturalistic, multi-animal cortical recording experimentally practical, and provides a broadly accessible technology for systems neuroscience.

title: Antarctic marine-based ice destabilized when warming outpaces solid-Earth feedbacks
abstract:
Delayed bedrock uplift can allow rapid warming to trigger Antarctic Ice Sheet retreat before classical instability thresholds are reached, lowering critical warming thresholds by up to 0.5 K in East Antarctica, according to coupled model simulations. 
 The Antarctic Ice Sheet is expected to be the largest contributor to sea-level rise over the coming centuries. Previous equilibrium ice-sheet simulations have suggested that this is due to crossing a bifurcation point associated with marine ice-sheet instability. Here we investigate whether sectors vulnerable to this instability can undergo rate-induced tipping, whereby rapid forcing and slow bedrock uplift trigger self-sustained retreat before the bifurcation point is reached. We test this with an ice-sheet model coupled to a glacial isostatic adjustment model, sampling the uncertainty in mantle viscosity. We find that slow bedrock adjustment weakens the stabilizing effect of glacial isostatic adjustment, allowing grounding lines to reach retrograde bed slopes more readily and triggering self-sustained retreat below the bifurcation threshold. Although the West Antarctic Ice Sheet is subject to a bifurcation, it is unlikely to experience rate-induced tipping because of the low mantle viscosity beneath the region. In contrast, the Recovery and Aurora subglacial basins are likely to undergo such a transition even under warming rates lower than those observed today. Depending on mantle viscosity, this mechanism can reduce the critical global mean temperature anomaly by up to 0.5 K, with important implications for the long-term evolution of the Earth system. title: Fatty acids in the tumor microenvironment reprogram neutrophils to induce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression in mice
abstract:
Lipid accumulation in solid tumors supports tumor progression by promoting immune evasion. Yet the molecular basis of this lipid-mediated immunosuppression remains unclear. Here, using murine models of advanced colorectal cancer, the authors uncover a metabolic-immune axis whereby tumor-derived fatty acids activate neutrophil PPARα, resulting in adenosine generation and T cell suppression. Importantly, treatment with a dual adenosine receptor antagonist restores T cell-mediated antitumor immunity and synergizes with anti-PD-1 therapy to enhance animal survival. 
 As solid tumors progress, the tumor microenvironment becomes increasingly immunosuppressive, impairing cytotoxic T-cell activity and limiting the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade. However, the mechanistic drivers of this immunosuppression remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a tumor-derived lipid–neutrophil–adenosine axis as a critical regulator of immune suppression in advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). We show that fatty acids enriched in tumor interstitial fluid reprogram neutrophils toward an immunosuppressive phenotype through PPARα activation, upregulation of CD39 and CD73, and adenosine generation, ultimately leading to T-cell suppression. AB928, a dual A2aR/A2bR adenosine receptor antagonist currently in clinical trials, restores T-cell proliferation, effector function, and tumor-killing capacity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, AB928 synergizes with anti-PD-1 therapy to enhance survival in an immunotherapy-resistant autochthonous model of metastatic CRC. Thus, our findings define a metabolic immune evasion mechanism in the microenvironment and provide a rationale for targeting neutrophil-derived adenosine signaling to improve immunotherapy responses in CRC. title: Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation
abstract:
The authors show that hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses generate terahertz emission in ZnTe through X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG). The findings establish a route to probing second-order X-ray nonlinearity and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids. 
 Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)—a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process—has not been experimentally observed until now. Here, we report the first observation of terahertz emission induced by hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses in solids, providing evidence for X-ray DFG. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. These results establish XFEL-induced terahertz emission as a general platform for probing second-order X-ray nonlinearities and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids. The findings establish a route to probing second-order X-ray nonlinearity and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids.

title: Human hemoglobin protects the parasite cytoskeleton during Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte development
abstract:
Wang et al. apply single particle cryo-EM to developing gametocytes of Plasmodium falciparum, and identify human hemoglobin as a prominent factor that binds to P. falciparum subpellicular microtubule (SPMT) network. 
 Transmission of Plasmodium falciparum requires the differentiation of asexual parasites into male and female gametocytes, which undergo extensive cytoskeletal remodeling, assembling a non-canonical subpellicular microtubule (SPMT) network. Using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, we determined structures of SPMTs isolated from developing gametocytes. Unexpectedly, we identified human hemoglobin as a prominent microtubule-associated factor that binds to P. falciparum SPMTs in a dimeric form rather than the canonical tetramer. Pharmacological perturbation of microtubules and hemoglobin isoform switching experiments demonstrate that this hemoglobin-SPMT association is essential for proper SPMT organization and gametocyte maturation. Together, these findings reveal a strategy by which P. falciparum repurposes a host metabolic protein to stabilize its cytoskeleton, highlight the intimate co-evolution between parasite and host, and suggest avenues to block malaria transmission. title: Anterior cingulate input tunes striatal dynamics for context-dependent social preference in a mouse model of autism
abstract:
The mechanisms underlying social behavioural deficits in mouse models of autism are not fully understood. Here the authors link neural embedding geometry to context-dependent social deficits in the Shank3 knockout mouse. 
 Social preference in autism spectrum disorder varies across contexts, but the underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Shank3 knockout (KO) mice, an autism mouse model, exhibit reduced preference for social over nonsocial stimuli while retaining a preference for females over males. Calcium imaging reveals context-dependent differences between KO and wild-type (WT) mice in the organization of neuronal population dynamics in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), corresponding to their behavioural preferences. Functional imaging and molecular analyses reveal reduced functional connectivity between the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and DMS and molecular alterations more pronounced in the striatal matrix. ACC inhibition eliminates genotype-dependent differences in DMS dynamics. Inhibiting the ACC–DMS pathway impairs social preference, whereas its activation in KO mice shifts DMS dynamics towards WT patterns and improves social preference. These findings identify a cortical pathway that shapes striatal population dynamics and context-dependent social preference in an autism mouse model. Here the authors link neural embedding geometry to context-dependent social deficits in the Shank3 knockout mouse.

abstract:

 Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to the limitation of structural design. Here we report a reactive processing strategy that creates heterogeneously dispersed nano-domains (hDNs) of rubbery ethylene-acrylic ester-glycidyl methacrylate terpolymer (EGMA) in polyoxymethylene (POM) matrix. Pre-reactive blending of EGMA with poly (L-lactide) (PLLA) and subsequent melt processing with POM result in formation of the unique morphology, where PLLA serving as the leveraging forces for opposing uniform distribution via chemical bonds and macro-phase separation by physical associations. The resulting materials exhibited optimized mechanical performance impossible to be acquired with conventional counterparts. This work identifies herein innovates how reactive processing can regulate phase morphology while balancing the trade-off among toughness, ductility, strength and stiffness in multicomponent polymer blends, representing a paradigm shift in narrowing gap between structure and tailor-made property towards pilot plant scale. title: Comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of energy inversion of the lowest singlet and triplet excited states in the heptazine HzTFEX<sub>2</sub>
abstract:
Through a comprehensive photophysical investigation, the conditions enabling the observation of phosphorescence from a substituted heptazine, HzTFEX2, have been elucidated so that the inversion of its singlet and triplet states is shown experimentally. 
 Detailed photophysical measurements of the non-symmetric heptazine, HzTFEX2, previously reported as having inverted S1-T1 levels, show complex behaviour, highly dependent on environment, concentration and aggregation. Here we show that, single crystals of HzTFEX2 show anti-Kasha S0←S2 and excimer emission. Solution state absorption shows a hypsochromic shift of the π-π* S0→S1, linearly dependent on solvent polarizability. In most environments, emission is dominated by excimer species, only in toluene and frozen 2-MeTHF do monomeric properties dominate. In frozen solutions, aggregation phenomena are solvent dependent. Given such complexity, time-dependent emission spectra are crowded, making it difficult to resolve monomeric phosphorescence. However, by exciting S0→S2 at 77 K, we observe a consistent phosphorescence signal at 425 nm, 110 ± 20 meV above the S0←S1 emission, whereas exciting S0→S1 does not give phosphorescence or delayed fluorescence (DF). We conclude that coupling between S2 and S1 is very weak, S2-TN intersystem crossing is effective, whereas S1↔T1 intersystem crossing is thermally activated, fulfilling the conditions required for the observation of inverted phosphorescence. At room temperature, no long-lived DF is observed because exothermic T1→S1 ISC becomes allowed, such that in an OLED, high efficiency can be achieved. Through a comprehensive photophysical investigation, the conditions enabling the observation of phosphorescence from a substituted heptazine, HzTFEX2, have been elucidated so that the inversion of its singlet and triplet states is shown experimentally.

How greenhouse warming affects such southward swings is not well understood. Here we show that, under a high-emissions scenario, the frequency of extreme southward swings doubles from one event per 22 years in the twentieth century to one per 10 years in the twenty-first century with an average increase in rainfall intensity of 20%. The increased frequency is related to faster warming of the African continent than of the Indian Ocean that intensifies northerly winds, and to a poleward migration of Southern Ocean westerlies that drives a pattern of faster subtropical Indian Ocean warming to the south and enhances Atlantic-to-Africa moisture transport, both of which favour a southward swing of the South Indian convergence zone. More frequent southward migration of the South Indian convergence zone might thus indicate increasing flooding risk in parts of southern Africa. Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone can lead to severe rainfall and flooding in southern Africa. Here the authors show that climate change leads to an increase in the frequency and intensity of such swings.

title: Functional diversity complements taxonomical diversity in productivity-biodiversity relationships in freshwaters
abstract:
Freshwater productivity–biodiversity relationships are predominantly unimodal, with stronger patterns in producers than consumers and lakes than rivers, according to a global analysis using phosphorus as a productivity proxy. 
 Productivity is widely considered a key driver of biodiversity, yet whether taxonomic and functional diversity respond similarly to productivity gradients remains unclear. Using phosphorus as an indicator for productivity gradient, we compiled 78 freshwater datasets spanning > 30,000 sites globally to test how productivity–biodiversity relationships (PBRs) vary across diversity dimensions, trophic groups, and ecosystems. We show that PBRs are predominantly unimodal across taxonomic and functional dimensions, with slightly weaker curvature for functional diversity. Unimodal PBRs are more pronounced in producers than in consumers and show stronger curvature in lakes than in rivers. Functional reorganization also varies along the phosphorus gradient, with the clearest contraction in resource-related trait space and marked shifts in community functional centroids. Climatic, geographic and human land-use gradients further modify PBR shape. These findings indicate that predicting biodiversity responses to productivity benefits from considering functional diversity, ecological context, and broad-scale environmental gradients. Freshwater productivity–biodiversity relationships are predominantly unimodal, with stronger patterns in producers than consumers and lakes than rivers, according to a global analysis using phosphorus as a productivity proxy.
